title: Resilience Gym: automated scenario executor and telemetry harness for Private VPCs
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
We need a safe, repeatable automation framework — dubbed 'Resilience Gym' — that can execute scheduled and on-demand multi-region switchover scenarios against Private (VPC) deployments. The goal is to exercise the end-to-end recovery path (routing, state sync, model fallback) while collecting detailed telemetry, and to validate upgrade/rollout procedures in a controlled fashion. This is not a generic chaos tool: it should be Terraform/IaC-aware, understand deployment topology (control plane vs data plane), and include preflight checks and guardrails so runbooks can be automated without risking data-plane corruption or violating compliance constraints.

Key components: automated scenario definitions (switch route, mirror traffic, simulate region outage), a scheduler + orchestrator that reuses customers' Terraform modules where possible, lightweight node validators and health probes, telemetry ingestion hooks for Console dashboards, and an audited execution log for compliance. The framework must support a simulation/dry-run mode that only exercises controllers and metrics without changing customer routing, and a gated execution mode that performs live switchovers with explicit approvals and automatic rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: Publish a Resilience Gym CLI that can run a scenario in dry-run and live modes against a target Private deployment
Create a Terraform module scaffold and examples demonstrating how to annotate resources (control-plane, compute, db) so the executor can perform safe cutovers
Implement preflight validators that abort if KV cache lag > threshold, model versions mismatch, or active jobs > threshold
Emit structured telemetry (trace + metrics + events) to Console so every scenario shows in a per-run dashboard
Provide automatic rollback if health checks fail within the configured grace period
Execution is auditable: all actions (approvals, steps, API calls) are logged to audit log with immutable IDs
work_items: Design Terraform annotation schema and update example modules in private-deployment-templates
Build lightweight validator library (python/golang) for preflight checks
Implement scenario orchestration service (k8s job or serverless) with pluggable executors for AWS/GCP/Azure
Wire telemetry exporters: traces to X-Ray/Jaeger, metrics to Prometheus, events to Console timeline
Add approval flow integration with Console (canary gate) and support email/Slack notification hooks
End-to-end integration test harness that runs dry-run then full-switchover in a sandbox account
notes: Keep live-mode defaults conservative: require explicit --confirm flag and an approval token from Console
Simulation mode should be the default for scheduled runs in prod namespaces until owner opt-in
Design terraform annotations to be opt-in: we cannot make assumptions about customer module shapes
We should reuse parts of ENG-30725's orchestration logic where applicable to avoid duplication
Security: execution service must use KMS for any temporary credentials and write to audit events with customer-owned keys if configured

2026-03-05: Validator prototype (kv-lag check) implemented in Golang; exposes HTTP /healthcheck with JSON output used by orchestrator
2026-03-08: First end-to-end dry-run passed in sandbox org-qa account. Telemetry traces visible in Jaeger; Console timeline received events but needs formatting
2026-03-10: Security sign-off requested. Added KMS key rotation note and requirement for customer-managed key option
review_feedback: PM (Sofia Morales): please add customer opt-out for scheduled rehearsals and ensure no PII is sent to Console telemetry
Design (Ethan Park): annotations look good; request a small UX flow in Console for approval tokens
SRE (Maya Chen): validators are necessary but add a conservative default for cpu/mem thresholds to avoid false positives during load spikes
implementation_notes: We will implement the orchestrator as a k8s-native controller in the private control plane when available; fallback to a serverless job in hosted control plane
Telemetry events must include scenario_id, step_id, resource_ids, and sha of terraform plan applied (if live mode)
Rollback strategy: phased rollback with configurable stages (control-plane first, then compute), and a final 'force-rollback' path for manual intervention
